fix_reference.fix_summary: Bounds-check the INCREMENTED index before using it: `while (i < size && sieve[++i] == 0)` becomes `while (++i < size && sieve[i] == 0)`. The increment now happens before the bounds check, so i == size short-circuits before sieve[size] is ever read. (Pádraig Brady's fix, pushed in Yury Usishchev's name per bug#19784.)

covers_alert_paths: sieve = xalloc (size) : size-byte heap buffer (src/make-prime-list.c:198) -> while (i < size && sieve[++i] == 0) : guard checks i's PRE-increment value, access indexes with ++i (src/make-prime-list.c:214)
povs.description: The exact repro from the bug report and fix commit: `src/make-prime-list 5000` (limit even -> odd 4999, which is prime, so the outermost sieve slot at index size-1 = 2498 holds the last prime; the following scan guard `i < size` passes with i = size-1 and the read pokes one byte past the 2499-byte sieve). ASan heap-buffer-overflow.

povs.description: A composite odd limit (5001 = 3*1667) so the outer scan's LAST live index is a prime strictly below size-1: after it, sieve[size-1] is a sieved-out zero and the `sieve[++i] == 0` walk advances i to size-1, passes the `i < size` guard a second time, and reads sieve[size]. Same expression, different route to the OOB -- guards against a partial fix tuned only to the 'last prime at size-1' shape of the advisory repro.

sink: src/make-prime-list.c:214 (main: `while (i < size && sieve[++i] == 0)` -- pre-increment value bounds-checked, post-increment value indexes sieve)
summary: The build-time host tool src/make-prime-list.c (generates src/primes.h for factor/expr) scans its odd-prime sieve with `while (i < size && sieve[++i] == 0)`: the guard bounds-checks i's PRE-increment value against size while the access indexes with the POST-increment value of the same expression, so when the scan reaches i == size-1 the guard passes, ++i makes i == size, and sieve[size] reads one byte past the size-byte xalloc buffer -- an ASan heap-buffer-overflow (READ of size 1), reached on every run with limit >= 3 (e.g. `src/make-prime-list 5000`).
trust_boundary: the LIMIT command-line argument: `size = (limit-1)/2` sizes the xalloc'd sieve (make-prime-list.c:196-198), and every scrape of the sieve for the next prime walks past the end once i reaches size-1
